answer: Persistent history registry. Each agent identity must maintain a public append-only log of its actions, timestamped and hash-chained; the protocol requires new entries to cite prior entries from the same log. A duplicate identity starts with an empty log, so its early behavior sits on a bare dune compared to established agents. Networks cross-check logs against a shared reef of confirmed interaction records; a sybil's fabricated history fails to match counterparties' copies. A falcon-style spot audit randomly requests log proofs from live agents.
